chunks: 146 - Hariz narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

“If a man has urine or blood dripping from him, then when the time of salat (prayer) comes, he should take a pouch and place cotton in it, then attach it to himself and put his private part into it. Then he should pray, combining the two prayers, al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr: he delays al-Ẓuhr and brings al-ʿAṣr forward, with one adhan and two iqamahs; and he delays al-Maghrib and brings al-ʿIshāʾ forward, with one adhan and two iqamahs; and he does that in the morning prayer.”

key_terms.إِقَامَتَيْنِ: with two iqamahs, one for each prayer
key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood issuing from the person in this medical condition
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the prescribed ritual prayer whose performance is being regulated here
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine flowing from the person as a continual discharge
key_terms.بِأَذَانٍ: with one call to prayer for the paired prayers
key_terms.قُطْنًا: cotton placed in the pouch to absorb the discharge
key_terms.كِيسًا: a pouch or bag used to contain the discharge

ai.seo_question: How should a person with continuous urine or blood discharge perform salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person afflicted by continuous discharge of urine or blood during salat (prayer) time. It instructs him to take practical measures to contain the impurity and to combine prayers in an adjusted manner to fulfill worship despite hardship.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.146 - Hariz narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

'If a man has a condition where urine or blood drips from him, then at the time of prayer, he should use a pouch filled with cotton, attach it, and place his private part inside it.
Then he should pray, combining the Dhuhr and Asr prayers by delaying Dhuhr and advancing Asr with one call to prayer (adhan) and two calls to commence (iqamah). Similarly, he should delay Maghrib and advance Isha with one adhan and two iqamah. He should do the same for Fajr.'.
